subject: Dedicated GPU pool options and pricing model — A100 / H100 / L40S tradeoffs
messages:
From: Erin Barnes <erin@finlytics.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@finlytics.com>, procure@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — initial info request

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re evaluating a dedicated GPU pool for our inference workloads (real-time chat + nightly batch embeddings). Procurement asked us to provide a shortlist of options so they can move to a commit. Can you share: 1) perf/$ tradeoffs between A100, H100, and L40S for 8k and 32k contexts, 2) recommended pool sizes for 5000 peak qps (p50 latency target 150ms), 3) commit tiers and associated discounts (12/36/60 months), and 4) any throughput guarantees or SLO language you offer on Dedicated?

We’ll attach your SOW to our procurement packet; an early spreadsheet with a TCO comparison would be ideal.

Thanks,
Erin
Erin Barnes
Director, ML Platform
FinLytics

[Attachment: FinLytics_requirement_brief.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Erin Barnes <erin@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — initial info request

Hi Erin — thanks, and great to hear you’re progressing. Short answer up-front: H100 gives best perf/$ at high sequence lengths and throughput, A100 is strongest for memory-heavy multi-model racks and is lowest-cost for predictable mid-run workloads, while L40S is attractive for cost-sensitive embedding-heavy workloads with large batch throughput but worse perf at tight latency SLOs.

I’ve attached a quick TCO workbook that models per-token and per-1k-req cost across commit tiers and GPU mixes (see TCO_A100_vs_H100.xlsx). Also attaching a drafter SOW with SLAs. High-level recommendations:
- If your p50 150ms is firm at 8k -> target H100 for the majority of the pool and mix in some A100s for large-model hostings (e.g., customer + system models).
- For 32k context runs (rare), reserve a small subset of H100s (or multi-GPU split) rather than sizing whole pool for worst-case.
- Commit: 36-month reserved pool at 70% utilization tends to hit the sweet spot for >$0.5M annual spend; discounts scale non-linearly with commit and pool size.

I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik to give a short sizing sketch and an annotated commit table.

—Sean
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

[Attachments: TCO_A100_vs_H100.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_SOW_template.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-04T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — internal sizing notes

Folks — I ran Erin’s example workload through our estimator: 5k peak qps with p50 150ms. Assumptions I used are in the workbook (batching, dynamic KV cache hit 30%, sequence length mix: 80% 8k, 20% 32k, avg tokens per response = 250).

Quick sketch:
- H100 80GB nodes (dense) -> ~45% lower latency at 32k vs A100 80GB; perf/$ better when >40% long-context. For your 80/20 mix, H100 wins overall by ~15% perf/$ vs A100.
- A100 80GB -> cheaper per-card and better for dense multi-model packing; if you need >10 concurrent long-context sessions per card, latency/p50 degrades.
- L40S 48GB -> cost-efficient for batch embeddings; for realtime must be heavily tuned (aggressive batching) and you’ll sacrifice tail latency.

Sizing (ballpark for p50 150ms target):
- Option A (H100-heavy): 40 H100s + 10 A100s (burst pool) -> target sustained throughput ~5.2k qps with headroom for spikes.
- Option B (A100-heavy): 60 A100s -> meets throughput but p50 pushes ~180–220ms on 32k runs unless we offload rarer long-contexts to H100 split.

Discounts: finance pushed that 25–30% list discount is achievable at commit levels we’re talking about; Naomi can confirm margin/cutoffs. Also propose a 6-month ramp credit and a 2% overage remediation credit if throughput SLOs missed during first 90 days.

Will prep a clean table for Erin tomorrow.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & pricing — finance & discount guidance

Quick note from finance: margin band target for Dedicated deals is 28–35% after discounts and estimated infra costs. For DL-2026-078:
- If FinLytics commits to 36 months and ~60-card equivalent (H100 equivalency) -> we can go to 28% list price (i.e., 28% off MSRP).
- 12-month commit -> cap at 18% discount.
- 60-month strategic commit -> open to 32–35% but requires Enterprise support add-on and SOC2/Custom SLAs.

Also want to flag network egress assumptions — FinLytics’ data flows to third-party analytics and will materially change unit economics; see attached Network_egress_assumptions.txt. Naomi can own a line item for egress in the quote.

-Naomi

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Erin Barnes <erin@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: H100-primary Dedicated pool + commit tier options

Erin — attaching a concise proposal and three commit-tier options (12/36/60) for your procurement packet. Highlights:
- Recommended baseline: 40 H100 + 10 A100 buffer (see explanation below).
- 12-month: 18% off MSRP; no throughput SLO credits; 6-week ramp window.
- 36-month: 28% off MSRP; 99.95% availability SLA on pinned routes; 90-day performance remediation credit (service credits up to 5% of monthly fees) if missed. Includes 25% ramp credits on first invoice.
- 60-month: up to 34% off MSRP; Enterprise support; custom on-prem options; guaranteed dedicated headroom policy (auto-burst reservations).

Sizing rationale (short): H100s handle 32k contexts without proportional latency surge; given your 20% long-context fraction, moving to H100-heavy mix reduces per-token cost by ~15% compared to an A100-only pool once caching and batching benefits are factored in. L40S would lower baseline spend by ~20% but would not reliably meet 150ms p50 for chat without aggressive batching — not recommended for user-facing chat.

Next steps: if the 36-month option looks reasonable, we’ll generate an LOI and legal can start SOW redlines. I’m happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement to walk the table.

Regards,
Sean

[Attachments: Redwood_SOW_template.pdf, TCO_A100_vs_H100.xlsx]

From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@finlytics.com>

Cc: Erin Barnes <erin@finlytics.com>, procure@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-11-10T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: H100-primary Dedicated pool + commit tier options

Sean / team — thanks for the detailed breakdown. Procurement ran the numbers and the 36-month package with the 28% discount plus the 90-day remediation credit looks like the best tradeoff for budget + performance. Two asks before LOI: 1) Can you confirm burst policy (how many cards will auto-burst and at what price?) and 2) We need a short paragraph in the SOW about how we’ll handle multi-region failover (we currently run in us-west and will want cross-region routing).

If you can add those clarifications, we’ll circulate an LOI internally and aim to sign week of 11/22.

—Rajiv
VP, Infrastructure (FinLytics)
